sections.heading: Admission Requirements
sections.content: Admission to Gordon College shall be open to Filipino citizens, both residents and non-residents of Olongapo City, Non-Filipino citizens, high school graduates, or passers of the high school equivalency certificate (PEPT). A non-resident is defined as any individual who has lived less than one year in Olongapo City, is not registered to vote in Olongapo City and/or does not pay property taxes or contributes to the economic development of Olongapo City.

sections.heading: New College Freshmen Students for Undergraduate Programs
sections.content: Admission to the chosen degree program will be based on an applicant’s Gordon College Admission Test (GCAT) results and previous high school/college academic records. Typical requirements: Original copy of High School Report Card (F138/SF9) or Original ALS Certificate of Rating Secondary Level for ALS Passers; Certificate of Good Moral Character; Copy of Birth Certificate; Medical Certificate (Issued by the Gordon College Clinic); Barangay Certificate of Residency; One 2x2 picture.

title: Continuing Students, Returnees and Cross Enrollment

sections.heading: Continuing Students and Returnees
sections.content: Continuing students are those previously enrolled but unable to enroll for at least one semester who decide to continue. Returning students requested transfer credentials but decide to re-enroll; returning students shall no longer be required to take the admission test.

sections.heading: Cross Enrollment
sections.content: GC students must get consultation and consent from College Deans; cross-enroll not allowed if subject/course is not open during last two semesters; request recommendation from Dean and authorization from Registrar. Students from other schools must present written permission from their school.

sections.heading: Getting Admitted
sections.content: Links to Freshmen, IGS, Transferees pages.

sections.heading: Admission Standards
sections.content: Applicants must meet general and specific standards. Minimum undergraduate GPA of 2.00 or 85% (except NSTP and PE). Students with lower averages may be admitted on probation with restrictions (max 6 units) and placed in full standing after achieving required grade point average. Specific programs have extra requirements (e.g., Master in Public Administration requires at least two years of government/public service; Master in Business Management accepts BS Commerce or BS Business Administration grads; other programs may require additional units or experience).

sections.heading: Requirements and Procedures
sections.content: Applicants must pass qualifying examination and interview. Applicants must submit Original Transcript of Records (with remarks 'Copy for Gordon College' or 'Granted Honorable Dismissal'); two ID pictures (2x2); Certificate of Employment (where applicable); Php200 non-refundable application processing fee; additional materials if required by program.
